sections.description:
Fixing a typo should not make a three-year-old article look brand new. Bulk Last Modified Locker keeps the last modified date of your published posts exactly where it was, no matter how many times you edit them.

There is nothing to set up per post. Activate the plugin and the lock applies to every published post of every public post type at once.

  • Applies in bulk — no per-post switch to remember, so nothing slips through
  • Covers every public post type, including custom post types added later. Exclude specific post types on the settings screen if you need to
  • Bump the modified date on purpose: tick "Bump the modified date on this save" in the block editor sidebar when an update deserves a new date. The tick applies to that save only and is never stored
  • Made a mistake? Reset the modified date back to the publish date from the posts list (bulk action or row action) or from the block editor sidebar
  • New posts still get a correct modified date when they are first published
  • Need the dates to move again for a while? Turn the lock off on the settings screen. The reset actions keep working while it is off, so you can still fix dates that already moved
  • No database tables and no scheduled events. Two option rows and a short-lived cache of the update information, nothing else
  • To check for updates, it requests a small file (info.json) from GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com), where the plugin is distributed. The request does not include your site's URL or any site data. It makes no other external requests
